body.statement: For every observed law \(P\in\mathcal M\) and every full-data law \(P^{\mathrm F}\) witnessing its membership, consistency, conditional exchangeability, strict overlap, continuity of the smooth observed regression version \(m\), and the maintained version convention \(\texttt{ass:potential-mean-continuity}\) imply \(\mu^{\mathrm F}(a,w)=m(a,w)\) for every \(a\in[0,1]\) and almost every \(w\) under the observed \(W\)-marginal. Consequently, for every \(a\in J\), \(\mathbb E_{P^{\mathrm F}}[Y(a)]=\theta(a)=\int m(a,w)p(w)\,dw\), so every admissible full-data extension of the same observed \(P\) agrees on the exact-dose causal curve over \(J\).
body.justification: This isolates the maintained continuous-version convention needed to identify a causal mean at every exact dose rather than only for almost every dose; the convention is not part of the excursion argument.
body.gap: Westling, Gilbert, and Carone (2020) develop the causal-isotonic estimand and identification framework; the exact jointly measurable continuous conditional-potential-mean version imposed here is an additional maintained convention rather than a condition attributed to that paper.
body.consumer: It gives the AHA/CMS nurse-hours profile and its threshold doses a causal interpretation under the maintained conditions.

obligation.what_is_open: The frozen assumptions do not connect fixed-dose exchangeability to the random diagonal \(a=A\), so the asserted exact-dose identification is false as stated.
obligation.obstruction: A jointly measurable potential-outcome process may have a spike only at the realized continuous dose. Such a spike is null for every fixed intervention, preserves the continuous conditional potential mean, and nevertheless changes the observed regression through consistency.
obligation.attempted: A finite-range quantization of \(A\) proves the lemma under the proposed diagonal \(L^1\)-continuity condition. The explicit spike witness verifies that some such diagonal regularity is genuinely needed.
obligation.partial_result:
The frozen assumptions do not identify the exact-dose curve.  Here is an explicit diagonal witness.  Let \(W\) and \(A\) be independent and uniform, let \(R\) be an independent symmetric random sign, and, for constants whose fixed bounds have interior slack, put
\[
 Y(a)=a+0.1R+0.1\mathbf 1\{a=A\},
 \qquad
 Y=Y(A)=A+0.1R+0.1.
\]
For each fixed \(a\), continuity of the dose law gives \(\Pr(A=a)=0\), whence \(Y(a)=a+0.1R\) almost surely.  Thus \(Y(a)\perp A\mid W\) for every fixed \(a\), and the jointly measurable version \(\mu^{\mathrm F}(a,w)=a\) is continuous.  Consistency holds by construction.  On the other hand,
\[
 m(a,w)=a+0.1,
 \qquad
 \theta(a)=a+0.1,
 \qquad
 \mathbb E_{P^{\mathrm F}}Y(a)=a.
\]
Moreover \(p=g=f=1\), \(r(a,w)=(a+0.1)^2+0.01\), and \(\kappa(a)=0.01\), so all primitive functions are smooth, overlap is strict, the observed curve is strictly increasing, and the variance is nondegenerate.  Choosing, for example, \(B=2\), sufficiently large \(L\), and compatible slope and variance constants places this law in an admissible instance of the frozen model.  Therefore pointwise exchangeability plus consistency and continuity of \(\mu^{\mathrm F}\) does not control the random diagonal \(a=A\).

The proposed diagonal \(L^1\)-continuity condition is sufficient and does not assume the desired equality.  Indeed, for a finite-range \(q_j\), pointwise conditional exchangeability may be applied separately to its finitely many values, giving
\[
 \mathbb E_{P^{\mathrm F}}\{Y(q_j(A))\mid A,W\}
 =\mu^{\mathrm F}(q_j(A),W).
\]
Conditional expectation is an \(L^1\)-contraction, so the proposed condition and consistency imply that the left side converges in \(L^1\) to \(\mathbb E_{P^{\mathrm F}}(Y\mid A,W)\).  Continuity of \(\mu^{\mathrm F}(\cdot,w)\), boundedness, and dominated convergence imply that the right side converges in \(L^1\) to \(\mu^{\mathrm F}(A,W)\).  Hence \(m(A,W)=\mu^{\mathrm F}(A,W)\) almost surely.  Strict overlap then gives equality for Lebesgue-almost every \(a\) and almost every \(w\); continuity of both dose sections upgrades it to every \(a\).  Integration against the normalized density \(p\) then yields the claimed causal equality.  This completes the proof once the proposed law condition is added to the model.
